theater: 色雷斯平原與特拉揚之門

battle.name: 894-896年拜占庭-保加利亞戰爭
battle.theater: 色雷斯平原與特拉揚之門
battle.brief: 八九四至八九六年，拜占庭皇帝利奧六世與保加利亞大公西梅昂一世爭奪色雷斯。八九四年拜占庭遠征軍在色雷斯被福卡斯擊潰，八九六年利奧六世御駕至布爾加羅弗貢，以方陣盾牆與塔格瑪騎兵大破保軍，迫其議和。卡牌兵器羅馬方陣盾的直系後裔斯庫托諾盾，正是擋住保加利亞輕騎的那面盾。

kit.name: 羅馬方陣盾
kit.history: 凸面的長方盾。羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚。

countries: 交戰雙方是東羅馬帝國（拜占庭）與保加利亞大公國（普雷斯拉夫帝國）。拜占庭以君士坦丁堡為都，國家機器建在主題制之上：色雷斯軍區、馬其頓軍區、亞美尼亞軍區等邊區民兵構成長期守備與徵召骨幹，首都周圍則有禁衛軍、學院軍、不死軍、御林騎士團四支近衛塔格瑪，以及由瓦良格人與北歐傭兵組成的親衛；君士坦丁堡本身設有造船廠、大兵器庫與軍械作坊，皇帝利奧六世可直接調撥精銳。海軍同樣是戰力的一部分，戰船可從博斯普魯斯海峽出動，在色雷斯與保加利亞黑海沿岸之間切斷敵後。保加利亞方面，首都為普雷斯拉夫，國家由可汗西梅昂一世執政，本是游牧部族聯盟演成的王國，已在八六四年由父王鮑里斯一世受洗而基督教化，並於八九三年召開普雷斯拉夫會議，宣佈教會脫離君士坦丁堡。其軍隊主力是與拜占庭重騎同樣講究速度的保加利亞騎兵，弓、馬刀與輕裝披掛為主，另有一支以重裝著稱、被編年史稱為阿科庫托伊的精騎。雙方的邊界是色雷斯平原、哈伊莫斯山脈的多瑙河渡口與黑海北岸一線，沿線分布德魯斯托魯姆、維米納西翁、辛吉杜努姆等要塞。這場戰爭的本質，是兩個帝國為同一條河與同一片河谷的爭奪。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were the Eastern Roman Empire, that is Byzantium, and the Bulgarian Grand Principality centred on Preslav. Byzantium had its capital at Constantinople, and its state rested on the thematic system: the theme levies of Thracesia, Macedonia and Armenia formed the backbone of permanent defence and of the annual mustering, while around the capital stood the four tagmata of the Excubitores, the Vigla, the Immortals and the Hetaireia, together with a personal guard of Varangians and other northern mercenaries. Constantinople itself had its dockyards, its great arsenal and its workshops, and the emperor Leo VI could draw on its finished weapons and moneyed crews at will. The navy mattered as well: warships could sail out of the Bosphorus and work the Thracian coast and the Bulgarian shore of the Black Sea. Bulgaria, ruled from Preslav by Khan Simeon I, had begun as a confederation of nomadic clans and had been Christianised in 864 by Simeon’s father Boris I, who was baptised with the name Michael; in 893 the Council of Preslav declared the Bulgarian church independent of Constantinople. The core of its army was the Bulgarian cavalry, which prized speed even more than the Byzantine heavy horse, fighting with bow, sabre and light equipment, and alongside it ran a heavily armoured elite recorded in the chronicles as the accoutoi. The frontier between the two states ran through the Thracian plain, the Danube crossings of the Haemus range and the northern Black Sea coast, lined with fortresses such as Durostorum, Viminacium and Singidunum. In essence the war was a struggle between two empires over one river and one river valley.
people: 皇帝利奧六世是這場戰爭的指揮核心。他於八八六年繼承巴西爾一世即位，此前已在邊境與阿拉伯人和保加利亞人周旋多年；他並非好戰之君，早年曾試圖以聯姻和外交套取西梅昂，甚至讓弟弟君士坦丁在婚姻與宗室問題上與保加利亞周旋。八九四年他派遣遠征軍，兵敗之後仍以皇帝身份兩度親征，最終在八九六年取得決定性勝利。拜占庭人因此給他一個不太客氣的綽號，殺手利奧（ὁ Ἀσωτός），而智者利奧是後世溫和的追稱。保加利亞方面，鮑里斯一世在西梅昂即位前一年被暗殺，這位受洗後取名米哈伊爾的基督徒可汗留下的是一個已經立國，卻仍受君士坦丁堡精神控制的國家。年輕的西梅昂接位後展現出極強的行政與宗教手腕，他在八九三年讓保加利亞教會獨立，組織翻譯經典，派遣學生到君士坦丁堡學習，這位少年皇帝在八九四年至八九六年的戰爭中既是統帥也是外交主角。將領層面，八九四年統兵的老尼古福羅斯·福卡斯是皇室的姻親、拜占庭最負盛名的老將，卻在色雷斯遭遇毀滅性打擊；八九六年真正贏下戰鬥的是他的長子巴爾達斯·福卡斯，這位身兼學院 Domestic 的重騎名將指揮著帝國最精銳的塔格瑪與近衛騎兵。同期活躍的還有亞美尼亞出身的將領約翰·庫爾庫阿斯，以及拜占庭派往保加利亞的使者馬努伊爾，他的報告讓君士坦丁堡得以判斷保加利亞的國力與信仰狀況。
peopleEn: Emperor Leo VI was the operational centre of this war. He had succeeded Basil I in 886, after years of frontier service against the Arabs and the Bulgarians, and he was not a warlike ruler by temperament: in his early years he tried to hold Simeon in check by marriage and diplomacy, and he even used his brother Constantine in marital and dynastic negotiations with the Bulgarian court. In 894 he sent out an expedition, and after its destruction he marched in person twice more, winning the decisive victory in 896. The Byzantines accordingly gave him an unkind nickname, Leo the Slayer, while Leo the Wise is the later, gentler epitaph. On the Bulgarian side Boris I was murdered a year before Simeon took the throne; the khan who had been baptised with the name Michael left behind a state that was already founded but still spiritually dependent on Constantinople. The young Simeon showed great administrative and religious talent, securing an independent Bulgarian church in 893, organising the translation of scripture and sending students to study in Constantinople; in the war of 894 to 896 this boy emperor was at once commander and diplomat. Among the generals, Nikephoros Phokas the Elder, who led the army in 894, was a kinsman of the imperial house and Byzantium’s most famous old commander, yet he was destroyed in Thrace. The man who actually won the fighting in 896 was his elder son Bardas Phokas, the Domestic of the Schools, who led the finest tagmata and guards of the empire. Also active in these years was the Armenian general John Kourkouas, together with Manuel, the Byzantine envoy sent to Bulgaria, whose reports allowed Constantinople to judge the Bulgar state’s strength and its religious condition.
kits: 本卡兵器是羅馬方陣盾（scutum），一件前100年前後的裝備：凸面長方盾，高可護住全身，寬足以與同袍肩並排相接。它的戰術價值不在厚度，而在盾緣互相咬合成一片連續的盾牆。對八九四至八九六年的交戰雙方來說，這面盾牌並非以原物參戰，而是以直系後裔的形式延續：拜占庭主題民兵斯庫塔托伊（skoutatoi）的名稱本身就來自持大盾者，其防禦裝備是從晚期羅馬方陣盾演變而來的長形大盾（skouton）與圓盾併用，重裝騎兵則配大圓盾（koulon）。拜占庭步戰核心從未真正放棄盾牆傳統，與保加利亞的每一次正面交鋒，都以方陣式盾線抵住衝鋒。同一體系裡的其他裝備同樣構成戰力底盤：步兵用短矛（kopidion）、標槍（cheirosiphon）與弓，鎧甲以鐵片札甲（klivanion）為主，富裕者加穿鎖子甲（lorikion）；騎兵用長矛（kontos）、彎刀與弓，甲胄為札甲或鎖甲；攻城方有大型投石機（helepolis、manganae）、人力扭索投石機、攻城塔與破城槌，904年圍困塞薩洛尼基時還留下扭索投石機的實錄。保加利亞騎兵以短而有力的反曲複合弓、馬刀、小圓盾與皮甲札甲為主，弓馬合一的機動性遠勝拜占庭重騎，編年史記載的阿科庫托伊則是其中甲胄最重的精騎。兩軍都大量使用標槍這類便宜而致命的投射兵器，戰場勝負往往取決於誰能把投射火力壓制到對方接近的距離。
kitsEn: The card shows the Roman scutum, a shield of about 100 BC: a convex rectangle, tall enough to cover the whole body and wide enough for two men to stand shoulder to shoulder. Its tactical value lay not in thickness but in the way one rim bit into the next, closing into a continuous wall of shields. For the two sides fighting in 894 to 896 this shield was not present in its original form; it survived as a direct descendant. The name of the Byzantine thematic infantry, the skoutatoi, itself means shield-bearers, and their defensive equipment grew out of the late Roman scutum in the shape of the long oblong skouton, worn together with round shields, while the heavy cavalry carried the large round koulon. The Byzantine foot never truly abandoned the shield-wall tradition, and every frontal meeting with the Bulgarians was decided by a phalanx-like line of shields. The rest of the equipment forms the same base of strength: infantry used the short kopidion, the cheirosiphon javelin and the bow, wearing scale armour (klivanion) with mail (lorikion) added by the richer; cavalry used the long kontos, sabre and bow, in scale or mail. The siege train had large artillery, the helepolis and manganae, traction trebuchets, siege towers and battering rams, and the siege of Thessalonica in 904 leaves a record of traction trebuchets in action. Bulgarian cavalry fought with short, powerful recurved composite bows, sabres, small round shields and light armour, and their bow-and-horse mobility far outstripped Byzantine heavy cavalry, while the accoutoi named in the chronicles were the most heavily armoured riders among them. Both armies threw vast quantities of javelins and similar cheap and deadly missiles, and the outcome of a field generally turned on who could suppress the opposing missile fire before the other side closed.
tactics: 八九四年的教訓決定了後兩年的打法。拜占庭遠征軍沿色雷斯大道推進時，隊形拉得太長，輜重與民兵同主力脫節，遭到保加利亞騎兵在開闊地帶包抄，步兵在無盾牆可依的亂戰中被衝散，全軍覆沒，只餘少數生還者退回拜占庭邊境。教訓是：在色雷斯的開闊平原上，絕對不能把主力和快速打擊的敵騎混在同一片地上行軍。八九五年利奧六世御駕東征，處置與前次完全不同：遠征軍只帶必要輜重，分隊行軍宿營，白天嚴格戒備，屢次避開保加利亞人挑起的野戰，改為逐一解除被圍的色雷斯要塞的圍困，同時以海軍在黑海沿岸騷擾敵後，切斷保加利亞的前後方聯繫。保住城、拖時間，等於把主動權一點一點收回來。八九六年的布爾加羅弗貢之戰是決戰。拜占庭軍隊在通往黑海的山谷中選擇陣地，地面狹窄，一側有河流與坡地限制機動；中央是持大盾的斯庫塔托伊盾線與其他主題步兵，兩翼是巴爾達斯·福卡斯率領的塔格瑪重騎與近衛騎兵，前方另有弓手與投射部隊。保加利亞軍依慣例以密集騎兵集群衝鋒，並使用佯退誘敵、馬上回身射擊的帕提亞射法；但地形與盾牌結成的牆把衝鋒速度吃掉，緊接著拜占庭重騎在近距離發起反衝，壓垮了密集隊形。追擊階段大量保加利亞兵在渡河時被淹死或被俘，西梅昂僅帶親兵逃向德拉斯特爾要塞，再由海路退回普雷斯拉夫。
tacticsEn: The lesson of 894 shaped the two years that followed. When the Byzantine expedition marched along the Thracian road its column was stretched far too long, the baggage and the theme levies fell away from the main body, and Bulgarian cavalry enveloped it in the open country, breaking the infantry in a melee where there was no shield-wall to stand behind; the army was destroyed and only a handful of survivors made it back to Byzantine territory. The lesson was plain: on the open plains of Thrace the main body must never manoeuvre in the same ground as enemy horse that strike fast. In 895 Leo VI marched east with an entirely different approach: the column carried only essential baggage, camps were taken in separate divisions, the army stayed under strict watch by day, pitched battle was repeatedly declined in favour of raising the sieges of Thracian fortresses one by one, and the fleet worked the Bulgarian Black Sea coast to cut the enemy's lines of supply. Holding towns and buying time was the way to recover the initiative inch by inch. The battle of Bulgarophygon in 896 was the decisive one. The Byzantines chose their ground in a valley leading to the Black Sea, where the terrain was narrow and a river and the slopes restricted manoeuvre on one flank; the centre was the line of skoutatoi with their large shields and the other theme infantry, the wings were the tagmata heavy horse and the guards under Bardas Phokas, with archers and javelin throwers in front. The Bulgarian host charged in the customary dense masses of cavalry and used the Parthian shot, feigning retreat and shooting backwards as they wheeled. But the ground and the wall of shields ate the speed of the charge, and the Byzantine heavy horse counter-charged at close quarters and broke the packed formation. In the pursuit many Bulgar horsemen were drowned or taken at the river crossings, and Simeon escaped with his own guard to the fortress of Drastar and then back to Preslav by sea.
data: 這一役留下的數字不多，但有幾個可以核對。首先是時間：戰爭於八九四年秋開打，各家編年史對確切月份記載不一，本檔取九月為起點，八九五年是拉鋸與圍城之年，八九六年是決戰與議和之年，和約則訂於八九六年或八九七年。其次是兵力的量級。編年史作者提到西梅昂的軍隊為以萬計的騎兵，並在八九四年至八九六年的戰役中出現大量阿科庫托伊式重騎；拜占庭方面則是數個軍區的野戰軍與首都塔格瑪同時出動，但沒有留下可信的頭盔數字，這類古代戰役的兵力記載多為修辭性的量級而非清冊，引用時只宜當作雙方皆以數萬計的對比。八九四年的敗仗則被一致描述為近乎全滅：老尼古福羅斯·福卡斯的遠征軍大部戰死與被俘，只有極少數回到帝國境內。第三是地理與距離：君士坦丁堡至亞德里安堡的道路約四百公里，亞德里安堡至決戰地帶約一百公里，決戰的山谷距黑海海岸數十里，西梅昂正是靠這段海岸線完成逃亡。帝國多瑙河防線上的德魯斯托魯姆、維米納西翁、辛吉杜努姆等要塞，是此後和約中爭議的關鍵點，和約還牽涉歲貢、俘虜遣返與土地割讓，細節各書記載互相矛盾，本檔只作定性描述，不作精確數字的斷言。
dataEn: The war left few hard numbers, but a few can be checked. First, the chronology: the war opened in the autumn of 894, though the chronicles disagree about the exact month, and this file takes September as the starting point; 895 was the year of feints, sieges and manoeuvring, 896 the year of the decisive battle and the peace, with the treaty concluded in 896 or 897. Second, the scale of forces. The chroniclers speak of Simeon’s army as cavalry numbered in the tens of thousands, and heavily armoured riders of the accoutoi kind appear in large numbers in the campaigns of 894 to 896. On the Byzantine side the field armies of several themes marched together with the tagmata of the capital, but no trustworthy head count survives: figures in ancient battle narratives are rhetorical magnitudes rather than muster rolls, and they are best used only to show that both sides fielded armies in the tens of thousands. The defeat of 894 is described consistently as near annihilation; most of old Nikephoros Phokas’s expedition was killed or taken prisoner, and very few returned to the empire. Third, geography and distance: the road from Constantinople to Adrianople runs some 400 kilometres, Adrianople to the battlefield about 100, and the valley of the decisive fight stands a few tens of kilometres from the Black Sea coast, a stretch of coast that carried Simeon away to safety. The Danubian frontier fortresses Durostorum, Viminacium and Singidunum became the points at issue in the peace settlement, which also concerned the annual tribute, the return of prisoners and the cession of land; the sources contradict one another on the detail, so this file describes them qualitatively and asserts no precise figure.
cause: 打起來的原因有多層，宗教與政治在最上層，經濟與地理在底層。最上層是八九三年普雷斯拉夫會議：保加利亞教會宣佈脫離君士坦丁堡的宗主教區，自設牧首，翌年君士坦丁堡以譴責與絕罰回應，等於把一次教會政治變成兩個帝國之間的國教衝突。西梅昂的目標並非單純脫離，而是要在教義、禮儀與文字上與拜占庭平起平坐，再以教會為骨幹，把保加利亞從部族聯盟徹底鑄成國家。第二層是鮑里斯一世突然身亡留下的權力真空。這位可汗生前剛完成受洗，剛與拜占庭建立姻親與教理上的關係，他的突然身亡讓親君派與親拜占庭派爭奪主導權；年輕的西梅昂選擇了強硬路線，同時在外交上把拜占庭推到對立面。第三層是地理與商業。色雷斯是東南歐的門戶，多瑙河渡口、通杜賈河谷地與通往黑海的海路都在這裡；控制色雷斯等於掐住拜占庭首都的腹地與歐洲腹地的通道，也掐住保加利亞人南下的商路與徵兵區。此外還有外來壓力：八九五年馬扎爾人跨過喀爾巴阡山進入多瑙河上游盆地，削弱了保加利亞在北方的屏障，拜占庭對這股北來力量有實際的縱容與利用。於是利奧六世要保色雷斯，西梅昂要南下爭霸，兩邊都沒有退讓的餘地。
causeEn: The war had several layers of cause, with religion and politics on top and economics and geography beneath. Uppermost was the Council of Preslav in 893: the Bulgarian church declared itself independent of the patriarchate of Constantinople and set up a patriarch of its own, and Constantinople answered the next year with anathema, turning what had been a matter of church politics into a conflict of state religions between two empires. Simeon’s aim was not mere separation but parity with Byzantium in doctrine, liturgy and script, and then the use of the church as the backbone to forge Bulgaria out of a tribal confederation into a state. The second layer was the power vacuum left by the sudden death of Boris I. The khan had only just been baptised, only just formed marital and doctrinal ties with Byzantium, and his murder left the pro-imperial and pro-Byzantine factions fighting for control; the young Simeon chose the hard line and at the same time pushed Byzantium into open opposition. The third layer was geography and commerce. Thrace was the gateway of south-eastern Europe, with the Danube crossings, the valley of the Tundzha and the routes to the Black Sea all lying in it; to hold Thrace was to pinch the throat of the Byzantine capital and the corridor into the European interior, and equally to pinch Bulgaria’s southern trade routes and recruiting ground. There was outside pressure too: in 895 the Magyars crossed the Carpathians into the upper Danube basin and weakened Bulgaria’s northern shield, and Byzantium actively encouraged and used that movement. So Leo VI had to keep Thrace, and Simeon had to push south to dominate; neither side had room to give way.
impact: 這場戰爭的結果是雙贏也是雙輸。對拜占庭，八九六年的勝利洗刷了八九四年的恥辱，卻是靠割地、按年歲貢與一份三十年的和約換來的；皇帝因此被拜占庭人叫作殺手，其後的君士坦丁七世寫作智者利奧，則是把同一個人的兩種評價分開擺放。實用層面上，這場戰爭把拜占庭的主題民兵體系推到了極限之後：靠方陣盾牆與塔格瑪重騎贏得的勝利，讓帝國看清了民兵與近衛混編、戰術紀律與地形選取的決定性，也推動利奧六世在九一二年把瓦良格親衛正式編為塔格瑪，令帝國在面對突厥系輕騎時多出一層可靠的衝鋒力量。對保加利亞，這是西梅昂一世治下國力與聲望的頂點：國家在八九六年之後成為南歐最具分量的基督教強權，主教區、修道院、書寫與翻譯事業全面展開，普雷斯拉夫成為與君士坦丁堡並列的基督教學術中心；雙方的三十年和平也讓西梅昂得以專心推行全國基督教化與行政整頓，國家因此擺脫了部族聯盟的舊質，進入長期穩定期。但八九六年的和平只是把衝突推遲，並未解決它。八九七年之後西梅昂與拜占庭關係轉為親密，甚至試圖聯手對付阿拉伯人；然而西梅昂的野心並未收縮，九一七年的阿凱洛洛斯與安希亞洛斯兩役讓保加利亞騎兵主力在兩天之內被打崩，最終九七一年君士坦丁七世之時，帝軍攻破普雷斯拉夫，保加利亞第一帝國就此崩解。八九四至八九六年的勝負，於是成了保加利亞兩百年國運的一個轉折點，而不是終章。
impactEn: The outcome of this war was a double win and a double loss. For Byzantium the victory of 896 wiped out the shame of 894, but it was bought with ceded territory, an annual tribute and a thirty-year peace; the emperor was accordingly called Leo the Slayer by the Byzantines, while Constantine VII’s later Leo the Wise sets the two verdicts on one man side by side. At the practical level the war pushed the Byzantine thematic system to its limit and past it. A victory won by a phalanx of shields and by tagmata heavy horse showed the empire that the mixture of theme levies and guards, of tactical discipline and choice of ground, was what decided such fights, and it pushed Leo VI in 912 to constitute the Varangian guard as a tagma, giving the empire one more dependable striking force against the fast Turkic horse. For Bulgaria the war was the summit of Simeon I’s state: after 896 the country became the most considerable Christian power in south-eastern Europe, with bishoprics, monasteries, writing and translation developing on a wide front, and Preslav rising as a Christian scholarly centre on a par with Constantinople; the thirty years of peace also let Simeon concentrate on the Christianisation and administrative reorganisation of the country, which freed the state from its old confederate character and entered a long period of stability. Yet the peace of 896 only postponed the conflict, it did not solve it. After 897 Simeon’s relations with Byzantium turned friendly, and he even tried to act with the empire against the Arabs; but his ambition did not contract, and the two battles of Achelous and Anchialos in 917 broke the main body of the Bulgarian cavalry within two days, until in 971 under Constantine VII the imperial army stormed Preslav and the first Bulgarian empire collapsed. The result of 894 to 896 thus marks a turning point in two centuries of Bulgarian statehood, not a final chapter.
result: 逐場看結果，脈絡清楚。八九四年秋，拜占庭遠征軍在色雷斯被保加利亞騎兵擊潰，老尼古福羅斯·福卡斯僅以身免，帝國在色雷斯的邊防幾乎崩解；西梅昂的騎兵一度深入到拜占庭城牆下，多瑙河渡口的堡壘接連告急。八九五年雙方拉鋸：利奧六世御駕東征，逐一解圍，並以海軍擾亂黑海沿岸的保加利亞補給線；西梅昂不肯打他選不中的仗，改用圍城與遊擊，試圖拖垮帝國遠征軍。八九六年，形勢在布爾加羅弗貢的山谷中決定：拜占庭盾線頂住密集騎兵衝鋒，塔格瑪重騎反擊擊潰密集隊形，追擊中大量敵軍被河水與俘獲所吞沒，西梅昂逃回普雷斯拉夫。和約隨即達成。據編年史記載，雙方議定三十年的和平；拜占庭割讓多瑙河下游的要塞德魯斯托魯姆及鄰近土地，並按年支付以白銀與絲織品計的歲貢；保加利亞方面則歸還基督徒俘虜，雙方約束軍隊不再越過色雷斯的界線。就當時而言，這是保加利亞在與君士坦丁堡的角力中取得的最大一次外交勝利：它承認了保加利亞作為獨立基督教國家的地位，同時把帝國的戰線往北推了回來。就長遠而言，這個結果並不穩固。西梅昂用三十年的和平換來國力，卻把帝國的注意力引向阿拉伯戰線，也讓保加利亞騎兵在沒有實戰消耗的情況下膨脹到九一七年無法收拾的規模；同一批編年史作者在八九六年為保加利亞大軍記下的無數騎兵，數年後在阿凱洛洛斯海灘上全數崩潰。八九四年到八九六年的戰爭最終只換來二十年的喘息，保加利亞的真正崩潰要等到九七一年。
resultEn: Taken battle by battle, the result is clear. In the autumn of 894 the Byzantine expedition was destroyed by Bulgarian cavalry in Thrace; old Nikephoros Phokas escaped with his life and little else, and the empire’s frontier in Thrace very nearly came apart, with Simeon’s horsemen riding to the walls of Byzantine cities and the Danube crossing fortresses falling one after another to alarm. 895 was a year of seesaw: Leo VI marched east, raising the sieges in turn and harassing the Bulgarian supply line along the Black Sea with his fleet, while Simeon refused to fight the battles he could not choose and fell back on siege and raid in the hope of wearing down the imperial army. In 896 the decision was made in the valley of Bulgarophygon: the Byzantine line of shields held the massed charge, the tagmata heavy horse counter-charged and broke the packed formations, and in the pursuit the river and the captives took a great part of the enemy host, while Simeon made his way back to Preslav. The peace followed at once. The chronicles record that the two powers agreed on thirty years of peace; Byzantium ceded the fortress of Durostorum on the lower Danube and the land around it and paid an annual tribute in silver and silk, while Bulgaria returned its Christian prisoners and both sides bound themselves not to cross the Thracian line again. For the moment this was the greatest diplomatic success Bulgaria had won in its long contest with Constantinople: it acknowledged Bulgaria as an independent Christian state and at the same time pushed the imperial frontier back to the north. In the longer term the result was not secure. Simeon bought strength with thirty years of peace, but he turned imperial attention towards the Arab front and allowed the Bulgarian cavalry to swell, without the attrition of hard fighting, to a size it could not manage in 917; the countless riders the same chroniclers credited to the Bulgar host in 896 were to break to the last on the beach at Achelous a few years later. The war of 894 to 896 bought twenty years of respite, and Bulgaria’s real collapse had to wait for 971.
